setting: a cozy kid bedroom at night, the same room as in the attached room picture if one is attached: soft warm peach walls, wooden floor, seen from a little further back and a little higher than eye level; a low wooden bed with a rounded headboard, small in the back-left corner against the back wall, its long side facing the viewer and fully visible, with a white pillow at the headboard on the left and a smooth lavender blanket, raised on short legs with a dark gap under its front side; a small warm glowing lamp on a little wooden shelf on the back wall between the bed's headboard and the window; a window in the middle of the back wall showing a dark blue night sky with a crescent moon and a few stars; a large open wooden floor with a big round cream rug in the middle and front of the room, in front of the bed; a rounded light-wood door at the back right with free wooden floor in front of it. Things look the same in every picture: the little woolly sheep is a small plush toy sheep: a round body of soft white curly wool, a cream face and cream ears, small dark-grey legs, dot eyes, a tiny smile and a little tuft of wool on its head, seen from the side, facing LEFT toward the bed; its back is about as high as a standing child's knee. The fence is one short piece of a low white wooden toy fence: three rounded posts and two rails, standing on the rug's right part, about as tall as the sheep's back, turned at an angle so it runs from the back toward the front, across the sheep's path from the door to the bed, about one sheep wide on the picture. No faces on the fence. Few things, soft warm lamp light, gentle shadows. No numbers, no digits and no text anywhere. The bottom-right corner of the picture is plain wooden floor with nothing important in it

Answer cards are drawn by the app from math.icon (the transparent sheep_stand layer) N times under a digit: no icon_* pictures. reference.bed: small in the back-left corner against the back wall, its long side facing the viewer and fully visible; headboard and white pillow at the LEFT end; lavender blanket smooth and flat; raised on short legs with a dark gap under its front side; the hero sits up in it (legs to the right under the blanket lump) from s1 to d2 and sleeps in it in end (spot on_bed; the end ambient_origin is her head, measured at staging)
reference.window: middle of the back wall, dark blue night sky, crescent moon, a few stars; Lulu flies in from here in s1
reference.lamp: small warm glowing lamp on a little wooden shelf on the back wall, between the bed's headboard and the window
reference.rug: big round cream rug filling the middle and front of the floor, in front of the bed: the sheep meadow (meadow_1-meadow_5 left to right, alternating a little back / front, apart, each sheep at least one tenth of the picture wide) lies on it; the fence stands on its right part, between the meadow and the door; spots measured at staging
reference.door: rounded light-wood door at the back right (right wall / back-right corner), fully in the picture; the waiting spots door_1-door_3 stand on the open floor in front of it, never on the door, door_1 nearest the fence, none in the bottom-right corner (plain floor, watermark); spots measured at staging
reference.sheep: props_sheep: a small plush toy sheep: a round body of soft white curly wool, a cream face and cream ears, small dark-grey legs, dot eyes, a tiny smile and a little tuft of wool on its head; seen from the side, facing LEFT (toward the bed); no other face details, no bell, no collar. On stage each standing sheep is about one tenth of the picture wide (about 160 px of 1600) and never smaller, so five fit apart on the rug; the curled-up sheep is just as long. Smaller than that a sheep is hard to count on a phone. All five sheep (parts sheep1-sheep5, counting order left to right) are the very same sprite. States: sheep_stand (on four legs) / sheep_sleep (the very same sheep curled up in a plump round ball of wool, about two thirds of the standing height, legs tucked in, head resting on its front, eyes closed, head to the LEFT, same size and angle). The sheet also has identical spares sheep_stand_2 / sheep_sleep_2: staging uses the cleanest standing sheep (also math.icon) and the sleeping sheep that matches it best. Per node (numbers change every play: a, b, c = a + b, d, e = c + d, e at most 5): s1 and s2 a sheep_stand waiting at door_1.. (none in the meadow), s2 they walk over the fence to meadow_1.. on 'qua hàng rào' / 'Over the fence' -> s3 a in the meadow, b more waiting at the door, arrive on 'qua hàng rào' / 'over the fence' -> c1, b1, a1: c sheep_stand in the meadow, nobody at the door -> n1 c in the meadow + d waiting at the door, arrive -> c2, e1, d1: e sheep_stand in the meadow, nobody at the door -> d2 each sheep switches sheep_stand -> sheep_sleep on its own number word ({count:e:sleep}) -> end: e sheep_sleep in the meadow. The rest of the five are hidden. The sheep hop on their numbers in every count; they never touch each other, the fence, the hero or Lulu
reference.fence: props_sheep fence: one short piece of a low white wooden toy fence: three rounded posts and two rails; no face; about as tall as the standing sheep's back, turned at an angle so it runs from the back toward the front, across the sheep's path from the door to the bed, about one sheep wide on the picture, like a little gate; one state, at the spot fence (about [0.67, 0.90], on the rug's right part, between the meadow and the door) in every scene; the sheep are drawn in front of it, so sliding across it reads as hopping over
reference.blanket: tidy_toys' props blanket_lump (lavender mound, folded back at the LEFT end): not used while she sits on the bed's front edge (s1 to d2 before 'yawn'; the room's own blanket lies flat behind her); over her body from d2 'yawn' / 'ngáp' (lie_yawn) and in end (asleep)

pictures.cover: Night, crescent moon in the window. {hero} sits on the front edge of the bed, facing the viewer, legs hanging down, bare feet dangling, smiling and pointing down at the rug in front of her. In the middle of the picture, on the round cream rug, exactly one little woolly sheep leaps over the small white fence: a small plush toy sheep: a round body of soft white curly wool, a cream face and cream ears, small dark-grey legs, dot eyes, a tiny smile and a little tuft of wool on its head, seen from the side, jumping toward the LEFT (toward the bed), all four legs tucked up in the air above the fence. The fence is one short piece of a low white wooden toy fence: three rounded posts and two rails, standing on the rug, about as tall as the sheep's back, turned at an angle across the sheep's path, the same fence as on the attached props sheet. Only this one sheep in the whole picture: no other sheep anywhere. Lulu floats in the air above the rug, between {hero} and the sheep, smiling and glowing softly; {hero}, Lulu and the sheep do not touch. No faces on the fence. No numbers, no digits and no text anywhere. The sheep and the fence stay well away from the bottom-right corner, which is plain floor. If a room picture or a props sheet is attached, the room, the sheep and the fence look exactly like in them
pictures.sticker: one little woolly sheep leaping happily over a small white fence: a small plush toy sheep: a round body of soft white curly wool, a cream face and cream ears, small dark-grey legs, dot eyes, a tiny smile and a little tuft of wool on its head, seen from the side, jumping toward the left, all four legs tucked up in the air above the fence, a happy look; the fence is one short piece of a low white wooden toy fence: three rounded posts and two rails, about as tall as the sheep's back; one small glowing yellow star rests on the tuft of wool on the sheep's head, touching it. The sheep, the fence and the star make one sticker shape. Nothing else: no child, no bunny, no numbers, no text

wide.prompt: Edit the attached picture into a new view of the very same room. Keep exactly the same cozy kid bedroom at night: the same soft warm peach walls, wooden floor, low wooden bed with a rounded headboard, white pillow and smooth lavender blanket, the bed raised on short legs with a dark gap under its front side, the small warm glowing lamp on the little wooden shelf, the window with the dark blue night sky, crescent moon and a few stars, the rounded light-wood door, the same colors, warm night lighting and soft 3D art style. Change only the camera: seen from further back and a little higher, so the whole room looks roomier. The bed is small in the BACK-LEFT corner, against the back wall, its long side facing the viewer and fully visible, headboard and pillow at its LEFT end. The window is in the middle of the back wall, the lamp shelf on the back wall between the bed's headboard and the window. The door is at the back right, on the right wall near the back-right corner, fully visible, with free wooden floor in front of it. A large open wooden floor fills about the lower 55 to 60 percent of the picture, with a big round cream rug in the middle and front of the room. The room is empty: no people, no animals, no toys, no fence, nothing on the floor or the rug, no sparkles on the walls, no text. Landscape 4:3 picture. The bottom-right corner of the picture is plain wooden floor with nothing in it.

hero_j.note: IMPORTANT: draw her FROM THE FRONT, never from the side. In every figure we see her face straight on, both eyes, and the whole front of her body, like a photo taken from right in front of her. She is SITTING, as if on the edge of a bed, but do NOT draw any bed, chair, box or floor: she sits on an invisible seat. Her knees are bent at a right angle and point toward us; her two lower legs hang straight down side by side; her bare feet dangle in the air. Her head is tilted down a little: she looks down at the ground in front of her, as if watching small toys on the floor. Same girl and same size in all four figures. Hands hold nothing.

props_sheep.note: Every thing is seen from the same angle: from the front, slightly from above; every sheep stands or lies side-on to the viewer, so its whole side shows, facing LEFT. No faces on the fence. All four sheep are the very same little woolly sheep at the same size, the same white wool, the same cream face and the same dark-grey legs, all facing LEFT; only the pose changes. Sizes compared with the standing sheep: the curled-up sheep is about as long as the standing sheep and about two thirds as tall; the fence is about as tall as the standing sheep's back and, turned at its angle, about as wide on the picture as the standing sheep. Draw exactly five things, well apart, in two rows: top row the standing sheep, the sleeping sheep and the fence; bottom row a second identical standing sheep and a second identical sleeping sheep (spares), the last cell empty. All four sheep are the very same sheep. No other sheep, no grass, no ground.
